This episode differs fundamentally from those past food safety actions because it is driven directly by explicit Supreme Court pressure and a hard mandate requiring a formal notification by a specific upcoming compliance hearing date, rather than discretionary administrative enforcement or routine regulatory crackdowns. Furthermore, unlike the localized e-commerce licence suspensions or specific spice bans, the current FSSAI proposal for red hexagonal warning labels targets ultra-processed foods on a systemic, nationwide scale with a direct judicial timer attached.

Unlike standard regulatory rollouts, the current dynamic mirrors the Centre seeking modifications or clarification when cornered by judicial mandates—seen in the recent Supreme Court approach regarding the OBC judgment—rather than executing final compliance. The reporting highlights FSSAI food safety crackdowns prompting internal audits and selective product prohibitions (such as Everest and Laljee Godhoo hing powder), which shows the agency is prone to piecemeal enforcement actions and interim bans instead of sweeping, finalized policy implementations under judicial countdowns. Therefore, the government is far more likely to seek further clarification or present partial, delayed drafts on September 10, 2026, failing to meet the strict threshold of a formal final notification.
